results.task: I have no pay yet this month. Rent is 900 and food is 300. Why do the percents of income not show? How are percents worked out?
results.reply:
Percents of income don't show because there is no income yet. A percent of income divides each spending line by total income, and you can't divide by zero. Once pay is entered, those percents will appear.

Here is how the percents work:

- **Percent of income:** each spending line divided by total income, as a whole number. Total income is the sum of the income lines.
- **Share of spending:** each spending line divided by total spending. This is the only set of percents shown this month. Rent is 75% of spending and food is 25%.

The percents are whole numbers, so they are rounded. They are also adjusted so they add up exactly. Each line first gets the whole-number part of its share. Any points still missing go, one each, to the lines with the largest leftover fractions. If two lines tie, the one higher in your list gets the point.

This month you typed $0.00 in income, $900.00 for rent, and $300.00 for food, so total spending is $1,200.00. More goes out than comes in, and the gap is $1,200.00. The numbers only count what you typed and don't say what you should do.
